survivingClaim: PROVED: Lemma I (each squarefull stratum is a signed sum, signs mu(d)mu(e), of sublattice sums Phi(j), j squarefull) and one-directional Proposition E (a power saving of |B| against sum_kappa |B_kappa| requires some squarefull j != 1, of norm up to Q, with N(j)^(1/2+eps)|Phi(j)| >= c Q^delta |Phi(1)|). MEASURED, for the finite trilinear estimator (rows 77-85% not common to its two halves) in the class-cell mean square at X = 1e6 and 1e7: the ratio of the signed sum over strata to the root sum of squares has exponent -0.005 / +0.001 in Q, equal to random-phase, conjugated, Liouville, THIN, random multiplicative and cubic rows within null scatter 0.003, stable under a shift of the conductor octave; r2 >= 0.72 at every point from the measured arrays. Not established: the converse of Proposition E; any statement for true sextic theta coefficients or a single target; that the squarefree share is more than the 93% row count. Closing lead 17 for squarefull stratification is supported by the two proved statements; the data add little weight. No eta, no abscissa, nothing about zeros.

Open as stand-alone routes: dual form on squarefree n; Type I on average over the level. The estimator is mostly non-polar remainder and samples no single target.

lesson: Stratifying rows by squarefull part is inclusion-exclusion over divisibility: it recombines bounded-level copies of the total and has no saving of its own. The assigned L1 ratio has a random-sign control that decays like 1/log Q (fitted exponent about -0.10), so it must be read against that control, not against 0. The estimator is mostly non-polar remainder (split-half correlation 0.14 at 1e6, 0.23 at 1e7), and the statistic is a family mean square that does not sample zero-carrying targets.
